forkContract: Vibestudio workerd storage and image preparation, task-scoped execution pins, native protected model request ports, canonical receipts and external continuation cancellation
Knowledge-only history imports, direct and nested tools, executable offer waves, dormant scheduling, bounded scheduler indexes and acknowledged host wake repair
Canonical task wait conditions and retained abort-handler ownership; source and tests use the fork contract without a compatibility runtime
notAdopted: Upstream orphaning of unavailable abort handlers: cleanup ownership remains retained and callers receive the original failure until the exact definition returns

Upstream Chord 1.3 and later host readiness and protocol changes require authenticated, incarnation-scoped dependency edges and cycle detection; timeout-based failure cannot establish lifecycle termination.
Upstream Durable sleeping/onWake and restart-limit contracts conflict with the fork’s single acknowledged wake and incident-repair contracts.
Per-model compaction overrides require carrying the admitted model into the child compaction when the protected request port changes selection.
